Release notes

Sourced from build_runner's releases.

package:build_runner v2.15.0

  • Remove --low-resources-mode as default memory usage has been improved. If you have problems with RAM usage please file an issue.
  • Remove --log-performance and --track-performance. File an issue if you have performance measurement needs not covered by the newer --dart-aot-perf.
  • Removed options can still be passed, they will be ignored with a warning.
  • Bug fix: fix crash during logging if an asset path is an invalid URI.
  • Bug fix: with --workspace the global options affecting build order were read from the wrong package. They are now read from build.yaml in the workspace root, like other global options.
  • Allow analyzer 13.0.0.

package:build_runner v2.14.1

  • Bug fix: fix crash if a package used to belong to a workspace but was removed from the workspace leaving a stale workspace.ref file.
  • Bug fix: the watch command now always does one build before exiting due to a request from another build_runner process. Fix crashes related to request before build start.

package:build_runner v2.14.0

  • Performance: further improvements to management of files for analysis for 2x faster incremental builds.
  • Performance: default to AOT compilation for commands other than run. This costs more initial startup time but gives faster builds afterwards. Fall back to JIT if the compile fails due to use of dart:mirrors. Use the --force-jit flag if you want the old default JIT builder compile. Use the --force-aot flag to turn off the fallback to JIT compile.
  • Add support for asset: scheme to the --build-filter flag. It is like package: but for the whole package, not just lib. For example, package:a/b.dart is the same as asset:a/lib/b.dart.
  • Paths specified using --build-filter when using the --workspace flag now apply to the current package, not the workspace root. Other packages must be referred to using package: or asset: schemes.
  • Add OSC 8 hyperlinks for logged input paths.
  • Better handling of deletions of files during the build: if the file is not needed ignore the deletion, if it's needed try to use the cached version, as a last resort restart the build.
  • Defer deletions of files by build_runner until the build is complete. Don't write files unless the contents changed. These reduce unnecessary work by tools that watch the filesystem.
  • --workspace flag is no longer experimental, remove the warning.
  • Add --workspace flag to clean command, use it to clear the cache used for a --workspace build.
  • Add new command stop: run dart run build_runner stop to terminate a running watch or serve command in the current package or workspace. If a build is in progress, the build will complete first.
  • Add locking: build_runner will wait for any already-running command before running. If there is an already-running watch or serve command, it will be closed after the currently-running build, as if you ran the new dart run build_runner stop.

Updates `flutter_secure_storage` from 10.0.0 to 10.1.0
Release notes

Sourced from flutter_secure_storage's releases.

v10.1.0

Android

  • Added storageNamespace option to AndroidOptions for full namespace isolation across storage instances (SharedPreferences, KeyStore aliases, config/key storage). Use this instead of sharedPreferencesName when running multiple FlutterSecureStorage instances with different cipher configurations.
  • Deprecated sharedPreferencesName in favor of storageNamespace, which provides complete isolation rather than data-only isolation.
  • Added migrateWithBackup option to AndroidOptions for crash-resistant migration. When enabled, backup copies of encrypted data are created before migration starts, allowing recovery if migration fails or the app crashes mid-migration. Works in conjunction with migrateOnAlgorithmChange.
  • Made KeyCipherAlgorithm and StorageCipherAlgorithm public enums.

Fixes:

  • Fixed crash on biometric failure (not error).
  • Fixed null safety issue in MethodRunner that could cause a crash on Android.
  • Fixed config being overwritten on initialization.
  • Fixed default Android key cipher not aligning with the Flutter default.

iOS / macOS

  • Added useSecureEnclave option to IOSOptions and MacOsOptions to store keys in the device's Secure Enclave for hardware-backed security.

Fixes:

  • Fixed kSecAttrSynchronizable being silently dropped when no access control flags are set.
  • Fixed readAll not returning Secure Enclave items correctly.

> Heads up: most of the diff is FRB codegen. Net total is ~7800 added lines; ~4300 of that is autogenerated `lib/src/rust/` and `rust/src/frb_generated.rs`, regenerated whenever the bridge surface changes. The hand-written review surface is ~1500 lines plus ~1700 lines of tests. Skim the codegen, read the rest.

This PR consumes the new `whitenoise_markdown::Document` AST from whitenoise-rs (pinned at `f421a8ad`). Chat bubbles now render CommonMark, GFM, and the nostr-extension format. Plain-text messages render byte-identically to before.

The marmots have learned to read bold text.

## What's in here

- `WnMarkdownText` walks the parsed AST and renders every Block and Inline variant.
- Plain-text fast path: single-paragraph messages with only Text/SoftBreak/HardBreak inlines skip the markdown renderer entirely. They keep the existing inline-timestamp layout.
- `@npub` mentions render as underlined `@DisplayName` (Vlad's design call). Tap opens a new in-app `UserProfileShade` instead of bouncing out to the OS. Non-npub Nostr URIs (note, nevent, nprofile, naddr, nrelay) still route externally because they point at events, not people.
- `SoftBreak` renders as a newline. The CommonMark default is a space, which loses every Enter press in the composer.
- URL scheme allow-list: `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `nostr`, `tel`. Anything else gets no tap recognizer at the renderer layer; the bubble's tap handler reapplies the same check before `launchUrl`. The Rust parser does not recognize HTML, so `<script>` and similar pass through as literal text.
- Surface boundaries: chat-list previews, reply quotes, notifications, and the composer keep their existing plain-text rendering.

## Bridge style

The bridge mirrors each AST type through FRB. The AST is FRB-friendly: owned `String`, `Vec<Enum>` recursion, `Clone`, `Eq`. Generated Dart sealed classes give exhaustive switch and IDE help. A hand-rolled Dart JSON parser would be a second markdown implementation and would drift from upstream.

## Tests + manual QA

- 4498 Flutter tests + 75 Rust tests pass. Coverage 99.03%. `just precommit` clean.
- Manual checklist run locally: every Block and Inline variant, surface boundaries, security cases (`javascript:`, `data:`, raw HTML stay inert), nested containers, CJK and RTL mixed runs, mention-tap into shade and back without scroll jump, long-press preview shows resolved names.

## Known limitations

1. Cross-inline highlight matches are not highlighted in search results.
2. Math renders as italic monospace source; no LaTeX engine is used.
3. Inline markdown images render as `[image: alt]` text links, not embedded.
4. Mentions of users outside the chat's metadata cache fall back to truncated npub until metadata loads. Follow-up could subscribe to mentioned pubkeys.

## Incidental upstream commits

The rev bump pulled in two non-markdown commits: `917ad14` (handle_contact_list lock contention) and `585d31f` (MDK update + push-token gossip). Both required adding `disappearing_message_secs: None` to two struct literals in `rust/src/api/groups.rs`.

title: fix: reset Whitenoise lifecycle after deleting data
body:
## Description

Fixes the reset lifecycle after deleting all app data. The bridge now replaces the process-global Whitenoise handle safely, waits for in-flight bridge calls before closing the old database, installs a fresh `Whitenoise::new(...)` instance before returning, and releases lifecycle permits before long-lived stream receive loops.

Also guards the start-DM flow after data reset by validating any cached DM group id before opening it. If the cached group no longer exists in Rust/MDK state, the app falls back to creating a fresh DM instead of opening a stale group and failing with `Group not found`.

Closes #660

title: feat(frb): consume whitenoise_frb from hosted pub server
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/c5c1a2e55045ff2c1ee8cb64efdf9cbb54632636fcb5a6926fa2848102e4f36f.png)

## What changed

This is the Flutter side of marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827. `rust_lib_whitenoise` now ships from whitenoise-rs as a published Flutter package on the `flutter-package` orphan branch, and this repo consumes it via a pubspec git dep. No more `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` runs locally, no more git-rev bumps after Rust API changes.

## Removed

- `rust/`: the wrapper crate. Canonical source now in `whitenoise-rs:crates/whitenoise-frb/`.
- `rust_builder/`: cargokit and plugin shape. Bundled inside the published package.
- `flutter_rust_bridge.yaml`: codegen config. Lives in whitenoise-rs.
- `lib/src/rust/`: auto-generated dart bindings. Published in the package.
- `justfile` recipes: `generate`, `regenerate`, `deps-rust`, `test-rust`, `test-rust-quiet`, `lint-rust`, `format-rust`, `check-rust-format`, `docs-rust`, `build-rust-debug`, `clean-bridge`, `clean-rust`.

## Updated

- `pubspec.yaml`: `rust_lib_whitenoise` switches from `path: rust_builder` to a git dep on `whitenoise-rs#flutter-package`.
- All Dart imports: `package:whitenoise/src/rust/...` becomes `package:rust_lib_whitenoise/src/rust/...` (191 files mass-rewritten; `dart fix --apply` re-sorted directives across 134 files).
- `analysis_options.yaml`: dropped the `rust_builder/**` exclude and suppressed `implementation_imports` because the orphan branch deliberately exposes `src/`.
- `AGENTS.md`: setup and dev sections rewritten, rust deps/test/lint references removed, and a pointer added to whitenoise-rs as the source of truth for the Rust core.

Stats: 304 files changed, 469 insertions, 47,854 deletions (mostly the deleted wrapper and generated dart bindings).

## Verified

- `flutter pub get` resolves the new git dep cleanly (1 dep changed).
- `flutter analyze`: No issues found.
- Dart import rewrite: zero residual `package:whitenoise/src/rust` references across `lib/` and `test/`.

## Coordination with whitenoise-rs

This PR pairs with marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#827, and order of merge matters: the whitenoise-rs PR lands (or its workflow runs via `workflow_dispatch`) so the `flutter-package` orphan branch contains the latest published package, then this PR can merge. Otherwise `flutter pub get` resolves an outdated snapshot. The wrapper sources in the orphan branch came from this branch's `rust/src/api/` (the singleton-removal refactor that is also in this branch's history).

## Why draft

The Android build script needs the follow-up above, and a manual smoke test of `flutter pub get` and `flutter analyze` from a clean clone is still pending before this is ready for review.

The colony has split the work across two burrows: one builds the bindings, the other consumes them. Less paw-ferrying for everyone.

title: Add native deep links for users, chats, and settings
body:
## Summary
- Added custom URI deep-link support for `whitenoise://` and `whitenoise-staging://` without introducing any HTTP redirect/server dependency.
- Routed `user/<npub>`, `chat/<groupId>`, and settings deep links through the existing GoRouter/auth flow, including post-login continuation to protected targets.
- Preserved pending deep-link redirects through the relay-resolution login path as well as normal complete-login path.
- Registered production/staging schemes in Android and iOS app config so each installed flavor handles its own links; Android flavors now own their scheme explicitly without a default production fallback.
- Updated profile sharing so QR codes encode profile deep links while copy text still exposes the plain npub.
- Updated npub scanning to accept supported deep-link QR payloads, including chat links, as well as bare npubs.
- Added a `Copy Deep Link` affordance to the chat raw debug screen so QA can copy a real `chat/<groupId>` link from a live chat.
- Excluded `settings/sign-out` from supported settings deep links.

## Deep link contract
- `whitenoise://user/<npub>` / `whitenoise-staging://user/<npub>` opens the user profile/start-chat surface.
- `whitenoise://chat/<groupId>` / `whitenoise-staging://chat/<groupId>` opens a single chat.
- `whitenoise://settings/...` / `whitenoise-staging://settings/...` opens supported settings screens, excluding sign-out.

## Testing
- `flutter test test/utils/deep_links_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/providers/deep_link_provider_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/routes_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/screens/login_screen_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/screens/relay_resolution_screen_test.dart`
- `flutter test test/screens/share_profile_screen_test.dart`

- `flutter test test/screens/chat_raw_debug_screen_test.dart`
- `bash test/scripts/release_automation_config_test.sh`
- `plutil -lint ios/Runner/Info.plist ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements`
- `xmllint --noout android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
- `just lint`

- `just precommit`

## Device validation
- Installed the staging build on Pixel 9a (`52281JEBF11805`).
- Verified Android resolves `whitenoise-staging://settings/notifications` to `org.parres.whitenoise.staging/org.parres.whitenoise.MainActivity`.
- Verified adb cold launch returns `Status: ok`.
- Manually verified settings, chat, and profile deep links on device.
